### Observed differences

- Activity A01 ran in about 46 in 100 traces in the earlier window (roughly 0.9 occurrences per trace) and is not observed in any of the 200 later traces; activity A13 is absent from the earlier window and runs in about 53 in 100 later traces (about 1.1 occurrences per trace). [OCC001, OCC010, POS001, POS012]
- The successor of A10 flipped completely: earlier, all 184 observed outgoing transitions of A10 went to A01; later, all 221 observed outgoing transitions go to A13. Correspondingly, A01 always led to A03 in the earlier window, while A13 always leads to A03 in the later window. [DIR001, DIR010, DIR011]
- The two activities occupy the same place in the trace: A01 earlier had a mean relative position of about 0.68 (median about 0.71), and A13 later has a mean of about 0.68 (median about 0.71). [POS001, POS012]
- A13 also relates to its neighbours as A01 did: earlier A10 preceded A01 in about 25 in 100 traces (interleaved in about 21), later A10 precedes A13 in about 23 (interleaved in about 31); earlier A01 preceded A11 in about 25 in 100 traces, later A13 precedes A11 in about 23. [REL009, REL073, REL010, REL075]
- Co-occurrence with the always-present activities switched sides: A01 co-occurred with A02, A03, A09 and A11 in about 46 in 100 earlier traces and never later, while A13 co-occurs with each of them in about 53 in 100 later traces. [REL001, REL002, REL008, REL010, REL022, REL032, REL070, REL075]
- The whole block also runs somewhat more often: A10's participation rose from about 46 to 53 in 100 traces, and A03's mean occurrences rose from about 1.9 to about 2.1 per trace, with A03 recurring in about 46% versus 53% of traces. [OCC008, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment A10 → A01 → A03 was replaced by A10 → A13 → A03: A01, which ran in about 46 in 100 earlier traces, always followed A10 and always preceded A03, is no longer observed, while A13 appears in about 53 in 100 later traces, is always reached from A10 and always leads to A03, at the same relative position and with nearly the same ordering relations to A10 and A11 that A01 had. The change is shown directly by successor evidence together with all-or-nothing participation differences that are maximally unusual under random re-splits of the two 200-trace windows, and the occurrence, direction, position and relation indicators all describe the same segment rather than independent effects. The replacement segment also appears in somewhat more traces (about 53 versus 46 in 100), visible as higher participation of A10 and slightly more recurrences of A03. The evidence cannot distinguish a genuine removal-and-insertion from A13 being a new label for A01's role, and the modest rise in how often the segment runs could still be sampling variation between the windows. [OCC001, OCC010, DIR001, DIR010, DIR011, POS001, POS012, REL009, REL073, REL010, REL075, OCC008, OCC002]

Other differences: A03's outgoing transitions shifted a few points from A11 (about 52% earlier, 48% later) toward A10 (about 48% earlier, 52% later); the fixed ordering between A03 and A02, A09 and A11 loosened slightly, with about 7 in 100 traces moving from the fixed order to interleaving; and A04, A05, A06 and A12 show small position shifts of a few hundredths. [DIR003, REL013, REL028, REL030, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS011]
